newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil products outlook - Rally hinges on US, Asia.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil products outlook - Rally hinges on US, Asia.

text.p: European oil products will be looking to Asia and the United States this week for the demand needed to bolster unexpectedly sluggish spring business at home, traders said.
Gasoline prices will key off U.S. demand but could edge higher while gas oil will again be well supported by strong Asian demand, provided vessels can be found to ship material.
The outlook for fuel oil is uncertain, with relative stability in the high sulphur barge price acting as a floor, even though cargo demand has begun its warm weather seasonal weakness.
"The market will stay on hold for a while until people see how U.S. May demand pans out," a gasoline trader said.
Gasoline demand is supposed to increase in the spring and summer, but last week's bearish U.S. inventory data, particularly for gasoline, continued to haunt traders.

However, there was stronger sentiment late last week with forecasts that gasoline will rally soon as the U.S. driving season begins. U.S. traders said poor weather in parts of the U.S. had slowed the start to spring.
The picture for naphtha remains bleak, with falling prices failing to draw petrochemicals to buy while uncertainty over gasoline direction dampens interest for reforming material.
Asia should continue to underpin the European gas oil market so long as there are enough ships to move material eastwards, traders say.
"Interest from the east remains, but there's an increasing problem of tonnage availability," said one trader, who expected 0.2 percent prices to ease if freight out of the area disappears.
"Local demand is pretty thin and there would be little pick up if we don't have this eastern draw," said a broker.
Russian material was expected to hover around May IPE +$2, while FOD and DIN were pegged steady at May IPE +$5 cif and May IPE +$4 cif respectively.
Diesel was expected to hold comfortably above May IPE +$10 cif NWE on the back of tight supplies and good buying interest, particularly into France.
Jet premiums may continue to crawl higher towards May IPE +$25 cif on the back of some April tightness, but supplies are set to improve in May, thus limiting gains.
High sulphur barges bounced around above $80 and $81 last week, with much higher bunker prices in Singapore supportive.
Their relative stability made traders wary of predicting sharp falls in high sulphur cargoes, even though the product should lose value as summer approaches.
Talk of cracked cargoes leaving the Mediterranean to the east may ease local over-supply but some brokers were puzzled prices had not already come down.
"High sulphur is due to die shortly. I'm not sure who or what is holding it up. It's a mystery in the Med," a broker said.
The low sulphur market looks weak, continuing to be dictated by Enel's falling demand and buying strategy. Straight-run still suffers from refiner's preference for processing cheap crude.
